title: Credit-card complaint routes can record monetary relief without showing consumer recovery
source_unit: CFPB public complaint API credit-card cases with company response labels
geography: United States; 15 states represented in the capped extract

denominator.unit: capped retrieval-order sample of published complaints routed to Credit card; required_sub_product=any

verified_consumer_recovery.unit: missing payment amount, receipt, adequacy, account correction, repeat effort, trust, switching, and exit

mechanism.value: A monetary-relief response label documents an institutional route and claimed remedy category, but not same-consumer receipt or repaired financial condition; absent public response fields also limit external visibility.

observations.method: Structured extraction from a de-identified CFPB public complaint API ledger. Cases are retained as administrative route observations; the capped retrieval-order sample is not weighted or treated as a representative complaint or remedy rate.
observations.uncertainty: The public records do not identify the monetary amount, payment receipt, account correction, adequacy, customer effort after submission, or later household outcome. A company response label is not proof of full recovery, and public_response_present is not a measure of consumer satisfaction or accountability.
observations.subgroup: Published 2026 credit-card complaints in the capped extract; 15 states are represented, with no demographic, balance, lender, amount, or outcome subgroup supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: The monetary-relief label may represent meaningful and timely recovery for some consumers, while the same administrative route can conceal uneven payment, unresolved account effects, or additional follow-up effort.

boundary: This record establishes observed complaint-routing and company-response labels in a capped 25-case extract. It does not establish monetary amounts, verified consumer recovery, representative prevalence, lender liability, causal effects, account correction, trust change, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact de-identified event ledger derived from the CFPB public complaint API; direct identifiers, company names, ZIP codes, and narrative text are omitted.
